mechanism_narrative: Sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC over the past three weeks (from -38.7% to -31.9%) indicates a consistent recovery trajectory independent of external shocks. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC higher than the baseline mean of the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6.8 percentage points over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of -34.5% observed in the prior 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 14.1% to 12.7% over three weeks) signals increasing willingness to leave home. This behavioral shift, combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM demand, indicates consumers are resuming discretionary retail visits as confidence grows, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 13% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 1.4 points over three weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 14% in week t+1 or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed -31.9% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed at -41.0%, indicating ongoing restrictions on public transport capacity or continued avoidance. If TRANSIT remains below -40% for the next two weeks, retail recovery will stall because commuting-dependent retail footfall cannot materialize, keeping RETAIL_REC flat or declining.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -40% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -41.0% in t-0w, unchanged from t-3w
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -35% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously exceeds -25%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered 17.4 percentage points over three weeks (from -39.1% to -21.7%), signaling a shift in outdoor leisure preferences and reduced lockdown severity. This outdoor activity recovery will substitute for indoor retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -22% and continues rising week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 17.4 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS declines below -25% in week t+1 or RETAIL_REC exceeds -28% despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility deteriorated sharply in t-0w (from -23.9% to -29.0%), a 5.1-point drop reversing three weeks of improvement. This sudden workplace collapse signals either new restrictions or behavioral pullback. When WORKPLACES falls more than 4 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC declines in the following two weeks due to reduced commuter-driven retail activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 4 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped 5.1 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -30% in weeks t+1 and t+2 despite WORKPLACES decline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -8% over three weeks, indicating essential shopping is resilient and baseline consumer engagement persists. When GROCERY_PHARM remains stable within a 3-point band, RETAIL_REC recovery accelerates because stable essential shopping signals confidence to resume discretionary retail, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance remains below 3 percentage points over two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged from -11.7% to -6.4% over three weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -12% or RETAIL_REC declines below -33% in the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising PARKS mobility (outdoor confidence) and declining WORKPLACES (reduced commuting) creates a substitution effect: consumers shift from commute-based retail to outdoor leisure. This dual shift suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as indoor retail loses both commuter and discretionary traffic to parks and home-based activities.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -22% AND WORKPLACES falls below -28%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -21.7% and WORKPLACES at -29.0% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds -28% in the next four weeks or PARKS declines below -25% while WORKPLACES recovers above -25%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of severely depressed TRANSIT (-41.0%) and elevated RESIDENTIAL (+14.1%) indicates policy-enforced mobility constraints. When TRANSIT remains below -40% and RESIDENTIAL remains above +13% simultaneously for two weeks, retail recovery is blocked because the policy regime prevents commuting and encourages home-based activity, suppressing RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -40% AND RESIDENTIAL above +13% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -41.0% and RESIDENTIAL at +14.1% in t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -35% or RESIDENTIAL falls below +12% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -30% despite both conditions holding.
